attributes.residual:
PREMISE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, FOR BOTH FUNCTIONS. The assignment (and the superseded label-correction record) held that the dead class caps ONE mr and that other structural rows - specifically the 5 and 6 CFG-BRANCH-TARGET rows regnorm reported - are separately reachable work. They are not: those branch rows are DERIVED ARTIFACTS of the single surplus instruction. Every one of them has the form `T
fn+0xN / O
fn+0x(N+4)`, i.e. a uniform +4 displacement of every branch target downstream of the extra copy, which is exactly what one extra instruction early in the body produces. Kill the copy and they all collapse together; they are not independently addressable and a control-flow or decl-order probe aimed at them is a guaranteed null. LoadWorldData (T85/O86, real 43): `--ops` gives `target-only: (none) / ours-only: -1 mr` - the ENTIRE opcode residual is one register copy. Its three clusters are one event, not three. Aligned head 0x0:0x34 shows ours completing `addi r0,r3,0 @lbl_80257680(ADDR16_LO)` at 0x0c - BEFORE the `stwu`/`stmw`, i.e. INSIDE THE PROLOGUE SHADOW - then copying `mr r31,r0` at 0x20 after the stmw, while the target keeps only `lis r3,@ha` in the shadow and writes the low half straight into callee-saved r27 at 0x18. This is FINDING 3 of the addrlo law reproduced exactly on a fresh instance: the ours-only `addi`/`lis` position clusters and the ours-only `mr` are two halves of ONE joint hoist-plus-copy decision, which is why the multiset nets to a single mr. LoadWorldDone (T84/O85, real 15): `--ops` gives `target-only: (none) / ours-only: -1 mr` with EXACTLY ONE cluster (insert O[8:9]@20 ['mr']). The aligned head 0x0:0x30 is `=` on every row through 0x18; at 0x1c the target writes `addi r28,r3,0 @lbl_8028C9A8(ADDR16_LO)` directly into callee-saved r28 while ours writes `addi r0,r3,0 @LO` then `mr r28,r0` at 0x20. There is no second mechanism anywhere in the function. This CONFIRMS attempt.loadworlddone-is-addr16-lo-via-r0-not-branch-shape.20260831.v1 in full; that record remains the live one for LoadWorldDone and no duplicate is proposed for it. DISPOSITION: both functions are correctly and completely capped by the accepted class law. Their `real` figures (43 and 15) are entirely the one surplus copy plus its downstream branch-offset shift, so neither is a candidate for further source work, and neither is WebFrank-eligible while ours is one instruction longer. The useful residual work in this lane is elsewhere in the two TUs.
